outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the inequality (sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues at most m + C(k+1,2), for every k) has been claimed proved in full by Kothari and Tudose (arXiv:2606.12197, first posted 10 June 2026, one version, no journal acceptance or public expert verification found by 11 October 2026); the claim is cited and used by several July 2026 preprints, and the separate Li–Guo equality ('full') version is claimed by two other July 2026 preprints; in the same period a k=3 case appeared in Linear Algebra and its Applications (2026) and several partial and approximate results were posted.
problem_asks: Part 1 (the only part the bullet names): for every simple graph G with n vertices and m edges, and for every k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n, the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues of G is at most m + C(k+1,2). The statement asks for an upper bound of this form for all k at once, so it has one family of inequalities indexed by k, over all graphs. The bullet does not ask for the equality characterisation of these inequalities (Li and Guo's 'full' conjecture, which asks when equality holds), nor for sharpness, nor for Laplacian energy; those appear in the literature as separate questions and are recorded below only where a result touches them.

events.what_happened: W.H. Haemers, A. Mohammadian and B. Tayfeh-Rezaie prove the k=2 case for every graph (S_2(G) ≤ m+3), and per the Wikipedia article the conjecture for all k on trees. First issued as CentER DP 2008-98; published Linear Algebra and its Applications 432 (2010) 2214–2221. I did not open the paper; the k=2 statement comes from a search summary and the trees statement from the fetched Wikipedia article.
events.revisions: CentER discussion paper 2008; LAA 2010 publication. Not checked for other versions.
events.delivers: k=2 for all graphs; all k for trees (per Wikipedia).
events.remains: All k ≥ 3 for general graphs.

checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal of record for spectral linear algebra
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper in 2010 (per Tilburg repository record seen in search; not opened)

events.direction: Supports the conjecture (proves it for k=2 and for trees).

events.what_happened: Brouwer verifies the conjecture by computer for every graph on at most 10 vertices. Cited by Wikipedia to Brouwer and Haemers, Spectra of Graphs (2012). The date of the computation itself is not established; the book is the earliest citable written source I found.
events.revisions: Not established.
events.delivers: Every graph with n ≤ 10 vertices, every k (finitely many instances of a claim about all graphs).
events.remains: All graphs with n ≥ 11.

machine_checked.system: computer enumeration (not described in the sources I read)

events.directly_checkable: Any finite graph with ≤ 10 vertices can be checked by computing its Laplacian spectrum; the source does not say how the enumeration was done.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture, for finitely many instances only.

events.what_happened: Zhibin Du and Bo Zhou, 'Upper bounds for the sum of Laplacian eigenvalues of graphs', Linear Algebra and its Applications 436 (2012) 3672–3683 (DOI 10.1016/j.laa.2012.01.007). Per Wikipedia, the conjecture holds for all k on unicyclic and bicyclic graphs, citing this paper. I did not open the paper.
events.delivers: All k, restricted to unicyclic and bicyclic graphs.
events.remains: Graphs with at least three independent cycles' worth of cyclomatic number, and all other graphs.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (per citation; not opened)

events.direction: Supports the conjecture within the stated classes.

events.what_happened: Rocha and Trevisan (Discrete Applied Mathematics, 2014) prove the conjecture for 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊g/5⌋, where g is the girth. Described in the 2026 Shamsher preprint's introduction; the Rocha–Trevisan paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: All graphs with 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊g/5⌋ (girth-bounded k).
events.remains: Larger k for graphs of small girth; all other graphs.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture within the girth-bounded range.

events.what_happened: X. Chen (Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2018) improves the girth range to 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊g/4⌋. Described in the Shamsher preprint; not opened.
events.delivers: All graphs with 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊g/4⌋.
events.remains: Larger k; all other graphs.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture within the girth-bounded range.

events.what_happened: Helmberg and Trevisan (Chemnitz preprint 2015; Linear Algebra and its Applications 2017 per search summary) define spectral threshold dominance and show that Brouwer's conjecture is equivalent to it; they prove the conjecture for split graphs and cographs. arXiv:1604.07867 ('Spectral threshold dominance, Brouwer's conjecture and maximality of Laplacian energy', April 2016) is attributed in one search summary to Stevanović and coauthors, in another to Helmberg and Trevisan; I did not open it. Authorship is unresolved.
events.revisions: Chemnitz preprint 2015; arXiv 1604.07867 (2016); LAA 2017 (per search summary).
events.delivers: Split graphs and cographs (all k); equivalence of the conjecture with spectral threshold dominance (a reformulation, not a resolution).
events.remains: General graphs.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for named classes; reformulates it as equivalent to spectral threshold dominance.
people: (co-author attribution unresolved; possibly Stevanović et al.)

events.what_happened: H.A. Ganie, S. Pirzada, B.A. Rather and V. Trevisan, 'Further developments on Brouwer's conjecture for the sum of Laplacian eigenvalues of graphs', Linear Algebra and its Applications 588 (2020) 1–18. Per Wikipedia: the conjecture holds for two large families, one built from a clique with each vertex identified with a vertex of an arbitrary c-cyclic graph, the other those whose maximal complete bipartite subgraph edges leave only c-cyclic components. Not opened.
events.delivers: All k, for the two named families of graphs.
events.remains: All other graphs.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for named families.

events.what_happened: Joshua Cooper, 'Constraints on Brouwer's Laplacian spectrum conjecture', arXiv:2003.03447 (March 2020, from the identifier). Per search snippets: partial bounds for low-arboricity graphs and for planar graphs with k ≥ 11, and bounds that hold unless the graph is far from a split graph. Wikipedia credits an n ≤ 11 verification to 'Cooper (2021), LAA'; the search snippets did not tie the 11-vertex computation to Cooper. I opened only the abstract-level material in search and did not check the small-graph section of the paper.
events.revisions: arXiv 2003.03447 (v1 March 2020); Wikipedia cites a Cooper (2021) LAA version; the relation between the two is not established.
events.delivers: Partial results for named graph classes and ranges of k (per snippets); the n ≤ 11 attribution is unverified.
events.remains: General graphs, all k.
events.doubts: Attribution conflict: Wikipedia (fetched) credits an n ≤ 11 extension to Cooper (2021); search snippets say the 11-vertex check comes from computer work cited by a 2025 paper, not from Cooper. Unresolved.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for named classes and ranges.

events.what_happened: Rocha (2020) shows the conjecture holds with probability tending to one for certain random graph sequences (per Wikipedia). The paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Asymptotically almost every graph in named random models (per Wikipedia).
events.remains: Every graph; the specific random models are not stated in the source I read.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture, in the probabilistic sense.

events.what_happened: Li and Guo (2022) study when equality holds in Brouwer's inequality and propose the 'full' conjecture: equality for some k iff G is a particular graph G_{k,r,s} built from a clique and two independent sets (per Chen and Zi's description). Li and Guo are also said to prove the full version for k in {1, 2, n−3, n−2, n−1} (per Chen and Zi, via search snippet). The Li–Guo paper itself was not located.
events.delivers: Proposes the equality (full) version; claims partial verification for the k values listed (as reported by Chen and Zi).
events.remains: The equality characterisation for other k. This is the Li–Guo question, not the bullet's inequality.
events.direction: Proposes a stronger (equality) form of the bullet's inequality; no counterexample reported.

events.what_happened: V. Blinovsky (2019 arXiv), later with L. Speranca and A. Pchelintsev, 'Proof of Brouwer's Conjecture (BC) for all graphs with number of vertices n > n_0 assuming that BC holds for n ≤ n_0 for some n_0 ≤ 10^24', arXiv:1908.08534 (identifier gives August 2019), published Russian Universities Reports: Mathematics (2025) per search snippet. The arXiv HTML I opened is v7 stamped 22 April 2025.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 Aug 2019 (month from identifier; v1 page not opened); v7 22 Apr 2025 (opened); journal version 2025 (per search snippet).
events.delivers: For n > n_0, the conjecture for all graphs, conditional on it holding for all n ≤ n_0 for some n_0 ≤ 10^24.
events.remains: Every graph with n ≤ n_0 (not established by the paper as stated); the conditional hypothesis itself.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2025 (per search snippet, not opened)

events.doubts: The result is conditional. The paper itself says it proves the conjecture 'under the assumption that it is true for all n ≤ n_0 where n_0 ≤ 10^24'. The base case is not verified by the authors in the text I read, and the search snippets did not show it verified.
events.direction: Conditional support for the conjecture for large n.

events.what_happened: Ke Wang, Zhen Lin, Shumin Zhang and Chengfu Ye, 'Brouwer's conjecture for the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues of some graphs', Open Mathematics 22 (2024) 402–410, DOI 10.1515/math-2024-0062. Per the DOAJ abstract snippet: upper bounds on S_k for graphs containing a friendship or book graph, and the conjecture for Halin graphs and some other classes. The De Gruyter page refused fetching (405) and the DOAJ page was not opened in full. The first public version may be earlier than the journal's October 2024 publication; I did not find a preprint.
events.revisions: Journal publication October 2024 (DOAJ). Earlier preprint not found.
events.delivers: The inequality for Halin graphs and for graphs with a friendship or book subgraph, over ranges of k the abstract states (not read in full).
events.remains: General graphs, and the rest of the k range for general graphs.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published (DOAJ and DOI record; full text not accessible to me)

events.direction: Supports the conjecture for named classes; the exact theorem statements are unverified.

events.what_happened: Slobodan Filipovski, 'A partial proof of the Brouwer's conjecture', arXiv:2412.12952 (17 December 2024, one version). The abstract says it proves the conjecture 'for all simple (m,n)-graphs' in two ranges of k: a first range for n ≤ m ≤ ((√3−1)/4)·n(n−1) and k between an explicit cube-root expression and n, and a second range that works for all (m,n)-graphs and k between an explicit square-root expression and an explicit upper bound in m and n. The exact formulas were restated by a fetch model and should be read from the PDF.
events.revisions: v1 only, 17 Dec 2024.
events.delivers: The inequality for all graphs with n vertices and m edges in the stated ranges of k (ranges depend on m and n; a subrange of k in each case).
events.remains: Every k outside the stated ranges, for every graph with m and n outside the first range.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture within the stated (m, n, k) ranges.

events.what_happened: V. Torres and V. Trevisan, 'Brouwer's conjecture for the cartesian product of graphs', Linear Algebra and its Applications 685 (2024) 66–76 (per the citing Lin–Wang paper). If the conjecture holds for two simple graphs, it holds for their Cartesian product. The paper itself was not opened and no arXiv version was located.
events.revisions: Not established; the first public version date (preprint or journal) is not found.
events.delivers: Closure: the conjecture for G1 and G2 gives the conjecture for G1 □ G2.
events.remains: The conjecture for graphs that are not Cartesian products of graphs already known to satisfy it.
events.direction: Closure property; supports the conjecture under a construction, does not settle it.

events.what_happened: Zhen Lin and Ke Wang, 'The preservation property of Brouwer's conjecture', Discrete Mathematics Letters 15 (2025) 39–45, DOI 10.47443/dml.2024.164. Received 15 September 2024, published online 17 March 2025 (per the journal record as cited). Studies whether certain edge-addition operations preserve the conjecture. Not opened; no preprint found.
events.revisions: No preprint found; the online date is the first public appearance I can establish.
events.delivers: Closure properties under edge-addition operations (per abstract snippet).
events.remains: The conjecture for graphs outside the closure construction.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published online 17 March 2025 (per the cited record; not opened)

events.direction: Closure property; does not settle the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Xiaodan Chen and Junwei Zi, 'More on the full Brouwer's Laplacian spectrum conjecture', arXiv:2503.11165 (14 March 2025, one version). Abstract: the full (Li–Guo equality-including) version holds for two families of spanning subgraphs of complete split graphs and for c-cyclic graphs with c in {0,1,2}; partial Nordhaus–Gaddum results. The paper states that Brouwer's conjecture is 'still open so far'. A journal version, 'On the full Brouwer's conjecture on Laplacian eigenvalues' by Chen and Zi, Discrete Applied Mathematics 391 (2026) 32–44, DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2026.04.036, published 6 May 2026 (OpenAlex record), is probably the same work but I have not confirmed that.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 14 Mar 2025 (only version listed). Probable journal version DAM 391 (2026), 6 May 2026 (unconfirmed identity).
events.delivers: The full (equality-including) form of the conjecture for the listed families only; nothing new for the bullet's inequality beyond those families.
events.remains: The full version for all other graphs; the inequality for general graphs.

checked_by.who: Discrete Applied Mathematics (journal), if the DAM 2026 article is this paper
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the 2026 article (identity with arXiv:2503.11165 not confirmed)

events.direction: Partial support for the full version; the bullet's inequality is not established beyond the stated families. Does not cut against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Oliver Knill, 'Remarks on the Brouwer Conjecture', arXiv:2508.07550 (v1 11 August 2025; v2 13 August 2025, 'corrected and more references'). Abstract: the conjecture holds for all graphs with n vertices when n ≥ 4 times the square of the maximum degree; also notes that the conjecture for graphs implies it for quivers. Per search summaries, Knill calls the problem still open and a twenty-year-old problem. The paper does not cite Kothari–Tudose (it predates it).
events.delivers: The inequality for all k, restricted to graphs with n ≥ 4Δ² (Δ the maximum degree).
events.remains: Graphs with n < 4Δ²; the full question for all graphs.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in a degree-restricted range.

events.what_happened: Alan Lew (Technion), 'An approximate version of Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture', arXiv:2601.17575 (24 January 2026, one version). Writes ε_k(G) for the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues minus the edge count. Proves ε_k(G) ≤ max over k-subsets U of |E(U)| + (4k−2)√k, hence ε_k(G) ≤ C(k,2) + (4k−2)√k; for K_{r+1}-free graphs a sharper form. Describes this as an approximate version of the conjecture ε_k(G) ≤ C(k+1,2). Per search summaries, published in the Journal of Combinatorial Theory B in 2026 (not verified).
events.revisions: v1 24 Jan 2026 only (as fetched). JCT-B 2026 publication per search summary, unverified.
events.delivers: An upper bound on the conjecture's own quantity ε_k, but with error term (4k−2)√k; it does not establish ε_k ≤ C(k+1,2).
events.remains: The exact bound ε_k ≤ C(k+1,2) for every k and every graph.
events.direction: Approximately consistent with the conjecture; does not settle the exact inequality. Cuts neither way on the exact claim.

events.what_happened: Shaowei Sun, Yaping Min and Kinkar Chandra Das, 'Sum of the k Largest Eigenvalues of Symmetric Matrices: Theory and Applications', arXiv:2605.26707 (26 May 2026; v2 29 May 2026). The abstract says the authors 'prove that the well-known Brouwer's conjecture holds for small values of k for almost all graphs' and call it a significant step toward complete resolution. Per search excerpts only: for k=3 the condition is m ≥ 3n+9 with n ≥ 4, plus k=4 and k=n−4 ranges. I read the abstract page only; the thresholds are unverified.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: the inequality for small k, for almost all graphs (the precise k-range and sense of 'almost all' not read).
events.remains: Large k; graphs outside the stated classes; the full conjecture.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in a restricted sense (small k, almost all graphs).

events.what_happened: Silin Huang, 'On a distance Laplacian analog of Brouwer's conjecture for several classes of graphs', arXiv:2606.06945 (5 June 2026 per the emergentmind aggregator). Proves a distance-Laplacian analogue of Brouwer's inequality for diameter-bounded graphs, diameter-2 graphs and graphs with large maximum degree. Recorded as an analogue event: it concerns the distance Laplacian, not the Laplacian.
events.revisions: v1 only (per aggregator).
events.delivers: Analogue only: the distance-Laplacian version for the stated classes. Says nothing about the Laplacian conjecture.
events.remains: The Laplacian conjecture is untouched by this paper.
events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet; an analogue.

events.what_happened: Ke Wang, Zhen Lin, Shumin Zhang and Chengfu Ye, 'A Proof of Brouwer's Conjecture for k = 3', Linear Algebra and its Applications 736 (2026) 189–213, DOI 10.1016/j.laa.2026.01.026 (title and bibliographic data from search results and a 2026 citation; the article page refused fetching). Per the fetched Wikipedia article, this 2026 LAA paper is the source for the cases t = 1, 2, 3 and t = n−4 through n holding for every n. The paper itself was not read. No arXiv preprint was found.
events.revisions: No preprint found; the online date (possibly January 2026, from the DOI's '01' component, unverified) is not established.
events.delivers: Per title: the inequality for k = 3 for all graphs. Per Wikipedia, also k = n−4 through n. Not verified against the paper.
events.remains: Per title and Wikipedia's list: k from 4 to n−5 for general graphs.

checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal of record in linear algebra
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (per DOI and citations; article page not accessible to me)

events.direction: Supports the conjecture for k = 3 (one value of the k-family); cuts in the direction conjectured.

events.what_happened: Pravesh K. Kothari and Stefan Tudose, 'On Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture', arXiv:2606.12197 (math.CO; submitted 10 June 2026; one version listed on the arXiv abstract page as fetched on 11 October 2026). The abstract states: 'We give a proof of this conjecture. Our proof relies on the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem for split graphs. We also show the converse, thereby establishing an equivalence between Brouwer's conjecture and the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem.' The HTML rendering lists Theorem 3.1 (Brouwer's Conjecture), Theorem 1.2 (Grone–Merris–Bai, general graphs), Lemma 3.2 (centred split-graph nuclear-norm bound), Lemma 3.3 (split-graph trace inequality), Lemma 5.1 (eigenvalue sums reduce to projections), Lemma 5.5 (a routing inequality) and Lemma 5.6 (for a rank-k projection P with P1 = 0, Lemma 3.2 implies Brouwer's conjecture); the text says 'We need the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem only for the case of split graphs.' The rendering garbled the formulas, so the argument itself was not read by me.
events.revisions: v1 only, 10 Jun 2026, as listed on the abstract page fetched 11 Oct 2026. No journal acceptance found.
events.delivers: Claims the full inequality: for every graph G with n vertices and m edges and every k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n, the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues is at most m + C(k+1,2). No restriction is stated in the abstract. Also claims the converse, so the conjecture and the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem for split graphs are equivalent.
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet's inequality, if the proof holds. The equality characterisation (Li–Guo's full version) is not part of the bullet and is addressed only by later preprints that rely on this paper.
events.doubts: No specific error, withdrawal or retraction found. One fact the later pass may weigh: the second author, Stefan Tudose, has no publication record I could find in several name-based searches (the matches were unrelated people), so his qualification is unestablished. This is not in itself a reason to doubt the argument.
events.direction: Proves the conjecture: cuts in the direction conjectured (the inequality holds for all graphs and all k).
people: Pravesh K. Kothari (Princeton University; per search snippets, computer science)

systems.name: GPT 5.5 Pro
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: used to simplify their proof that Brouwer's inequality implies the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem (the converse direction of the equivalence), and used for proofreading the manuscript. The disclosure does not say the model supplied any idea or argument.
systems.basis_quote: We used GPT 5.5 Pro to simplify our proof that Brouwer’s Inequality implies the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem. We also used it for a proofreading of our manuscript.

events.what_happened: Dongxiu Cai, Zhengbo Chen, Jia Yang and Xiao-Dong Zhang, 'The Equality Cases For the Laplacian Conjecture of Brouwer', arXiv:2607.03388 (v1 3 July 2026; v2 10 August 2026). Abstract: Kothari and Tudose 'proved the Brouwer's conjecture' in 2026, and the authors, 'motivated by their perfect proof and methods', characterise equality: for 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1, s_k(G) = m + C(k+1,2) exactly when G is a threshold graph with clique number k+1. They state this confirms the full Brouwer conjecture of Li and Guo (2022). The inequality is taken from Kothari–Tudose; this paper's own result is the equality characterisation.
events.revisions: v1 3 Jul 2026; v2 10 Aug 2026 (content of v2 read via the HTML rendering; no change to the equality statement noted).
events.delivers: The equality characterisation for the inequality (a stronger form than the bullet's inequality, and the Li–Guo full version); relies on Kothari–Tudose for the inequality itself.
events.remains: For the bullet's inequality: nothing beyond Kothari–Tudose. For the full Li–Guo version: claimed complete by this paper, subject to the Kothari–Tudose inequality.

checked_by.qualification: Authors of a parallel equality-case paper in the same area
checked_by.what_they_did: Note that their Lemma 2.3 overlaps with Lemma 15 of this paper and both rely on the projection method of Kothari–Tudose; they describe their own scope as different. This is a comparison of arguments, not a stated verification of this paper.

events.doubts: The equality claim is a second, independent-looking route to the same characterisation as Cui and Chen (July 2026); no referee report or journal acceptance found. The paper's proofs rely on the Kothari–Tudose inequality, so this paper is only as sound as that result.
events.direction: Claims the equality characterisation, and so the full Li–Guo version; not the bullet's inequality.

events.what_happened: Yuhang Cui and Xiaodan Chen, 'Characterizing the equality case in Brouwer's inequality for Laplacian eigenvalues', arXiv:2607.17293 (v1 19 July 2026). Same equality characterisation as arXiv:2607.03388 (threshold graph with clique number k+1, for 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1). The authors say the characterisation, 'together with the confirmed Brouwer's conjecture, would yield a complete solution to the full Brouwer's conjecture posed by Li and Guo (2022)', and that their proof relies on the projection method of Kothari and Tudose. Their 'Declaration of AI Use' is recorded below.
events.revisions: v1 19 Jul 2026 only (as fetched).
events.delivers: The equality characterisation (full Li–Guo version) for all n; relies on Kothari–Tudose for the inequality. Not the bullet's inequality.
events.remains: For the bullet's inequality: nothing beyond Kothari–Tudose. The authors do not claim to prove the inequality themselves.
events.doubts: The paper relies on the Kothari–Tudose inequality and reuses its projection method; the equality claim is therefore conditional on that result for its full-conjecture conclusion. No referee report or journal acceptance found.
events.direction: Claims the equality characterisation (full Li–Guo version), conditional on the inequality; not the bullet's inequality.

systems.name: GPT 5.5 Pro
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: used to simplify their proof for Lemma 2.4 of the equality paper. Does not say the model supplied an argument or idea.
systems.basis_quote: We used GPT 5.5 Pro to simplify our proof for Lemma 2.4.

events.what_happened: Jing Huang and Chunyan Qin, 'A Matching-Number Refinement of Brouwer's Laplacian Eigenvalue Inequality', arXiv:2607.07118 (v1 8 July 2026). Prove Lew's conjecture that the additive term in ε_k(G) ≤ kν(G) + ⌊k/2⌋ can be removed in the non-endpoint range: ε_k(G) ≤ kν(G) for 1 ≤ k ≤ n(G)−2, where ν is the matching number and n(G) the number of non-isolated vertices; they also characterise equality. The paper cites Kothari and Tudose: the Brouwer inequality 'was recently proved in full by Kothari and Tudose [13]', and its Lemma 5.1 uses that bound.
events.revisions: v1 8 Jul 2026 only.
events.delivers: A matching-number bound on ε_k for 1 ≤ k ≤ n(G)−2 (a bound on the conjecture's own quantity, with a different right-hand side). Not the inequality with C(k+1,2).
events.remains: The bullet's inequality, which this paper does not state as its result.
events.direction: Neighbouring bound on ε_k; does not change the status of the exact inequality; relies on Kothari–Tudose for its Lemma 5.1.

events.what_happened: Junying Lu and Jiabao Yang, 'Proofs of two conjectures on generalizations of Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture', arXiv:2607.08452 (v1 9 July 2026; v2 12 July 2026). Prove two conjectures of Lew (matching-number and vertex-cover-number upper bounds on ε_k) 'using Brouwer's Laplacian inequality', which the abstract says was recently confirmed by Kothari and Tudose. The acknowledgements say Conjecture 2 was 'proved independently and concurrently by Huang and Qin'.
events.delivers: Two bounds on ε_k in terms of matching and vertex-cover numbers, conditional on the Kothari–Tudose inequality. Neighbouring; not a new resolution of the bullet's inequality.
events.remains: The bullet's inequality, which this paper uses rather than proves.
events.doubts: Conditional on the Kothari–Tudose inequality; the result is only as sound as that result.
events.direction: Neighbouring; relies on the bullet's inequality as a tool.

events.what_happened: Dongxiu Cai, Zhengbo Chen, Jia Yang and Xiao-Dong Zhang, 'The Equality Cases for the Grone–Merris–Bai Theorem', arXiv:2607.23583 (v1 26 July 2026). Per search summary, determines the equality cases of the Grone–Merris–Bai inequality for each k (two families obtained from a threshold graph by a local modification). The HTML I read says the paper's key tool is the split-graph trace inequality of Kothari and Tudose (Lemma 3.3 of arXiv:2606.12197), that 'Kothari and Tudose proved Brouwer's conjecture by applying this inequality', and that 'our proof follows the structure of [6]'.
events.revisions: v1 26 Jul 2026 (as fetched).
events.delivers: Equality cases of the Grone–Merris–Bai inequality, a neighbouring theorem; not Brouwer's inequality. Relies on Kothari–Tudose.
events.remains: The bullet's inequality, which this paper does not claim.
events.direction: Neighbouring result on the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem; not a verdict on Brouwer's inequality.

events.what_happened: Seyed Ahmad Mojallal, 'A proof of the maximum Laplacian energy conjecture for connected graphs via a sharp eigenvalue-sum bound', arXiv:2609.06442 (6 September 2026). Proves a sharp bound on S_k for n/2 < k ≤ n−2 on connected graphs and, combined with 'Brouwer's inequality', the Vinagre–Del-Vecchio–Justo–Trevisan maximum Laplacian energy conjecture. The abstract calls the bound 'complementary to Brouwer's inequality' and does not claim the bullet's inequality.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: A sharp bound on S_k for the stated k-range, for connected graphs; a different question (energy). Uses Brouwer's inequality as an input; it is not stated whether it cites Kothari–Tudose.
events.remains: The bullet's inequality is not addressed by this paper.
events.direction: Neighbouring energy result; uses the bullet's inequality without stating which source it relies on.

events.what_happened: Tahir Shamsher, 'A maximum matching based refinement of Brouwer's conjecture', arXiv:2609.12673 (11 September 2026, one version). Proves the conjecture for 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊ν(G)/2⌋ (ν the matching number), hence 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊n/4⌋ for graphs with a perfect matching; gives a complement reformulation. The paper refines Rocha–Trevisan (k ≤ ⌊g/5⌋) and Chen (k ≤ ⌊g/4⌋). The HTML introduction says 'Numerous partial results have been established in support of Brouwer's conjecture' and does not cite Kothari–Tudose or the July 2026 papers. Whether it states the conjecture as open is not explicit in the text I read.

summary: The bullet asks whether Brouwer's inequality, that the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues of a graph is at most its edge count plus C(k+1,2) for every k, has been settled. The record I could assemble is as follows. Through 2025 the problem was open in the sense the literature used (Chen and Zi, March 2025, say 'still open so far'; Knill, August 2025, the same), with partial results for named graph classes, girth- and matching-based ranges, and degree-restricted and asymptotic results; Blinovsky's arXiv proof (2019; published 2025) is conditional on a finite verification up to 10^24 vertices, which the paper leaves open. On 10 June 2026 Pravesh K. Kothari and Stefan Tudose posted arXiv:2606.12197, whose abstract says 'We give a proof of this conjecture', relying on the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem for split graphs and proving the converse. If that proof holds, it is the event the problem's status would rest on. I could not verify it: the PDF came back as compressed binary, and the HTML rendering gave me the lemma titles and the AI section but garbled formulas, so I have not checked the argument; the record rests on the authors' abstract and on later papers that cite and use the result. Those later papers (Huang and Qin, 8 July; Lu and Yang, 9 July; Cai et al., 3 July and 26 July; Cui and Chen, 19 July) cite, use or state the inequality as confirmed; none of them is an independent verification of the Kothari–Tudose argument. Two September 2026 preprints (Shamsher, 11 September, partial results only; Mojallal, 6 September, energy) are the only later work I found that does not cite it. No journal acceptance, referee report, public expert commentary, or Lean formalisation of the Kothari–Tudose argument turned up in my searches (two of them targeted Lean); the second author has no publication record I could find. Separately, Wang, Lin, Zhang and Ye's paper 'A Proof of Brouwer's Conjecture for k = 3' (LAA 736, 2026) settles the k=3 instance for all graphs, per its title and the Wikipedia citation; I could not open it. On AI: the only AI disclosure I found bearing on the inequality is the Kothari–Tudose statement that GPT 5.5 Pro was used to simplify their proof that Brouwer's inequality implies the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem (the converse direction) and for proofreading. Under §5.4 that is simplification and proofreading, so it is not obviously load-bearing for the inequality, but the converse is part of the paper's claimed equivalence and the disclosure says the model simplified 'our proof', which means a human argument existed; I have recorded it in ai.systems with the quote and left the weighing to the later pass. Cui and Chen also disclose GPT 5.5 Pro for simplifying Lemma 2.4 of their equality paper. I found no AI credit in any other paper I read in full text, and abstract-only checks on the rest show no AI statement. I found no lab announcement, AI-results tracker or press item that credits an AI system with the Brouwer result. Close calls: (1) whether the Kothari–Tudose preprint should count as a resolution depends entirely on the correctness of an argument I could not read; (2) whether the Li–Guo equality conjecture is part of the bullet (I treat it as not asked, since the bullet asks for the inequality); (3) whether Lew's 2026 approximate bound, which does bound the conjecture's own quantity ε_k with an error term, moves the problem (I record it as not settling the exact inequality).
competing_reading: Read the Kothari–Tudose preprint as a resolution. The claim is specific, the reduction is to a classical theorem (Bai's Grone–Merris proof, TAMS, per search snippet) for split graphs, the converse is stated as well, and three later groups have built on it as confirmed. Read as such, the bullet is solved in June 2026 by a human-authored argument whose only AI contribution, on the authors' own account, is simplification of the converse and proofreading, so no AI system contributed to the result itself. Against this, the claim rests on one 11 KB preprint with no referee report or public verification in about four months, a second author with no traceable publication record, and later papers that use the inequality as a tool without checking it, so their 'confirmations' are one reliance chain. If the simplification of the converse changed a step that the main argument depends on, the AI contribution is load-bearing, and the record cannot tell which.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A referee report, or acceptance in a named journal, of arXiv:2606.12197, or a written verification by a specialist in spectral graph theory or majorisation (for example, an author of the Grone–Merris, Bai or Helmberg–Trevisan work). (b) A line-by-line check of Lemmas 3.2, 3.3, 5.1, 5.5 and 5.6 and of the reduction from general graphs to split graphs, which I could not read; or a Lean/Coq formalisation with no sorry. (c) The authors' account of what GPT 5.5 Pro's simplification changed in the converse argument (before and after versions), and whether any step of the inequality proof was produced or altered by the model. (d) Confirmation of the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem for split graphs against Bai's published version, which I did not open. (e) For the Wang–Lin–Zhang–Ye k=3 paper, its own abstract and theorem statement, and any arXiv preprint. (f) The Stefan Tudose publication record or institutional affiliation, which I could not find.

event.what_happened: Pravesh K. Kothari and Stefan Tudose, 'On Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture', arXiv:2606.12197 (math.CO; submitted 10 June 2026; one version listed on the arXiv abstract page as fetched on 11 October 2026). The abstract states: 'We give a proof of this conjecture. Our proof relies on the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem for split graphs. We also show the converse, thereby establishing an equivalence between Brouwer's conjecture and the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem.' The HTML rendering lists Theorem 3.1 (Brouwer's Conjecture), Theorem 1.2 (Grone–Merris–Bai, general graphs), Lemma 3.2 (centred split-graph nuclear-norm bound), Lemma 3.3 (split-graph trace inequality), Lemma 5.1 (eigenvalue sums reduce to projections), Lemma 5.5 (a routing inequality) and Lemma 5.6 (for a rank-k projection P with P1 = 0, Lemma 3.2 implies Brouwer's conjecture); the text says 'We need the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem only for the case of split graphs.' The rendering garbled the formulas, so the argument itself was not read by me.
event.revisions: v1 only, 10 Jun 2026, as listed on the abstract page fetched 11 Oct 2026. No journal acceptance found.
event.delivers: Claims the full inequality: for every graph G with n vertices and m edges and every k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n, the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues is at most m + C(k+1,2). No restriction is stated in the abstract. Also claims the converse, so the conjecture and the Grone–Merris–Bai theorem for split graphs are equivalent.
event.remains: Nothing of the bullet's inequality, if the proof holds. The equality characterisation (Li–Guo's full version) is not part of the bullet and is addressed only by later preprints that rely on this paper.
event.doubts: No specific error, withdrawal or retraction found. One fact the later pass may weigh: the second author, Stefan Tudose, has no publication record I could find in several name-based searches (the matches were unrelated people), so his qualification is unestablished. This is not in itself a reason to doubt the argument.
event.direction: Proves the conjecture: cuts in the direction conjectured (the inequality holds for all graphs and all k).

judgement.why: The statement asks for the inequality S_k ≤ m + C(k+1,2) for all graphs and all k; Kothari–Tudose claim exactly that with no restriction, so scope is whole; it is an unrefereed preprint with no named expert reading, so unreviewed. Credibility stays credible: Kothari is an established researcher, the method is a concrete reduction to Grone–Merris–Bai for split graphs, no error is identified, and several independent groups build on it; Tudose's untraceable record and Shamsher's non-citation are not enough for doubt (Shamsher plausibly missed a three-month-old preprint). The GPT 5.5 Pro disclosure covers simplifying an existing human proof of the converse (not the bullet's inequality) and proofreading, which produced no mathematics in the result, so ai_role none; likewise Cui–Chen's simplification of their own Lemma 2.4. Equality characterisations (Li–Guo full version), Lew-type matching/vertex-cover bounds, the distance-Laplacian analogue and the energy result are different questions, so variant. Lew's approximate bound bounds the conjecture's own quantity with an additive error and is a bound. Closure properties and Blinovsky's conditional reduction are none; Brouwer's n ≤ 10 enumeration is instances. Year-only 2024 dates (Open Mathematics, Torres–Trevisan cartesian) are null; year-only 2026 dates are necessarily after the snapshot.
judgement.doubts: The Kothari–Tudose argument was never read by the researcher (garbled formulas); the whole/credible call rests on the abstract and on downstream papers that rely on it rather than verify it. The k=3 LAA paper's exact range (only k=3 vs. also k=n−4..n) is unverified. Torres–Trevisan 2026 'critical index' content is unknown; scored none for lack of evidence. Rocha 2020 'almost all random graphs' scored variant since probabilistic statements settle no restricted class.
